_what: Community Care (love.css §122): the street's room for asking. Its channel on the CB is where anybody signed on asks for mutual aid, peer support and any other help, and where anybody who can offers it. Ryan's brief, 2026-10-22, built from three pages of ours: Community Care (stimpunks.org/aid/community-care/), our glossary's Peer Support, and Tuesday Ferguson's Tapping the Radical Roots of Peer Support. Read by tools/make-community-care.py, which writes the canopy, the four things the channel is for, every section with a quotation in it, who reads the channel, next door, and the credits, into community-care.html and liner-notes.html.
_quotes: EVERY QUOTATION WAS READ OFF ONE OF OUR OWN PAGES, named in `read_on`, and is checked against the Knowledge System mirror's copy of that page word for word on every build where the mirror is on the machine: the Town Hall's rule. When our page changes, re-copy the quotation; never loosen the check. Somebody else's words on our page carry who said them and the work they come from, and the room says they were read on our page rather than in the original, the Community Library's rule. Where our page names nobody's work, `work` is empty and `unnamed` says so: the herbarium's rule, so nothing is filled in from memory.
_cap: A QUOTATION IS AT MOST `words` WORDS, and the number is printed in the room. Covenstead's reason rather than the Zibaldone's: these are a handful of passages the room's own words are about, and the longest is a defining sentence. Raise it on purpose, here, with the reason written down, never to fit one passage.
_umbrellas: THE ROOF IS EVERYBODY'S UMBRELLAS, TIED TOGETHER. The tool draws the canopy from this list, left to right along the front row, with a back row behind it offset by half an umbrella; each colour is one of the room's own declared inks by name. It refuses two umbrellas alike side by side, four in a row in a rainbow's order (the Dopamine Dress-Up Den's rainbows are on its wall, not here), and an umbrella with no tie to the next one: nothing holds this roof up but the ties.
_no_charity: NOBODY IS SORTED. The tool refuses the vocabulary that sorts people who ask for help -- deserving, worthy, needy, the less fortunate, the vulnerable, beneficiaries, handouts -- in the room's own words, with the negation window, so the room can still say that nobody is sorted. Nothing For Sale's rule, in the room where people ask in their own names.
_no_debt: NOBODY OWES ANYBODY. It refuses pay it forward, repay, owe you, in return, give back, debt and a favour owed, with the negation window: help that puts somebody in debt is a loan with a smile on it, and the mutual aid category in our own forums says nobody owes anybody.
_no_tally: NOTHING IS COUNTED. No total of what was asked or given, no list of who helped most, no wall of thank-yous, no goal and no progress bar. A room for asking is exactly where a counter of good deeds would arrive as a kindness.
_no_proof: NOBODY PROVES ANYTHING. It refuses the vocabulary of a means test -- proof of need, verify, evidence, eligibility, qualify, documentation -- with the negation window. The Foundation's own grants have an application and the room says so and links it; the channel has none.
_crisis: THE ROOM SAYS IT IS NOT A CRISIS LINE, near the top, and links where the crisis lines are. The tool refuses the page without that paragraph, because a channel full of people offering help is exactly where somebody in danger might wait for an answer.

four.name: Asking
four.line: Say what you need, in your own words, as much or as little as you like. Nobody asks you to prove it, to say how you came to need it, or to have tried everything else first. Asking is not a weight on the room: it is how the people who want to show up find out where to stand.

four.name: Offering
four.line: Offer what you can spare, when you can spare it, and on your own terms. Nobody keeps track of who offered and who did not, and an offer that turns out to be more than you have can be taken back.

four.name: Receiving
four.line: Take what is offered without paying for it in gratitude. Thanks are welcome and never owed, and nobody keeps a note of who has had help, or how often.

four.name: Declining
four.line: Either side can say no. An offer that does not fit can be turned down, an ask can go by, and nobody is asked for a reason. A no is an answer, not a verdict on anybody.

four.p: That is the whole of what the channel is for, and all four of them are allowed here. The line is off a slide in Vivian Ly’s talk at Autscape 2020, which our own Community Care page carries, and which is here to press as well.

solidarity.p: Mutual aid is people meeting each other’s needs directly, sideways rather than downwards. Nobody in here is the giving kind or the needing kind, because most of us are both, often in the same week, and the umbrella you are standing under today is not the one you brought.

Stimpunks also makes [mutual aid grants](https://stimpunks.org/aid/grant/) and [creator grants](https://stimpunks.org/creators/grant/) to neurodivergent and disabled people. Those are the Foundation’s, by application, in scheduled rounds, and they cannot cover anything urgent; their own pages say whether they are open, who they can reach and what they cannot pay for. Asking in this channel is asking the community, not applying, and you can do both.

peer.p: Tuesday Ferguson wrote that for our blog in 2024, as a youth peer support worker, about what becomes of peer support when it turns into a job inside the systems it grew up resisting. [The whole essay](https://stimpunks.org/2024/05/08/tapping-the-radical-roots-of-peer-support/) is better than anything this room could say about it. What the room takes from it is where peer support comes from:

So nobody here is assessed, referred or signed up for anything. Peer support in a channel is somebody saying that happened to me too, and this is what helped, and staying. Nothing has to come of it that anybody else can measure:
Our glossary’s entry on [peer support](https://stimpunks.org/glossary/peer-support/) starts by naming the version this is not:

Nobody in here is buddied up with anybody to learn how to pass. The research the entry gathers says what Autistic people kept asking for instead, and it is honest about what being a peer does not give you:
This room keeps that second line. Being a peer is not the same as knowing what to do, nobody in here is pretending to be a service, and the entry says what peer support is for beside the rest:

woven.p: Our Community Care page opens with those two, and then with the story the dominant culture tells about care: that needing help is weakness, that independence is a virtue, and that your survival is your own problem.

That is what the umbrellas are. Nobody brought enough for everybody, and nobody had to. Every umbrella is tied to the ones beside it and to the shopfronts either side, nothing else holds the roof up, and not one of them keeps anybody dry by itself. The ties are drawn from a line of Sophie K. Rosa’s, which our page carries too:

not_here.name: No proving it.
not_here.line: Nobody asks for a diagnosis, a story, a reason or evidence, and nobody decides whether a need is real.

not_here.name: No sorting.
not_here.line: Nobody here is the deserving kind or the other kind. Everybody under the umbrellas is somebody who might ask.

not_here.name: No ledger.
not_here.line: Help puts nobody in anybody’s debt. Nothing records who gave and who got, and receiving costs nobody a performance of gratitude.

not_here.name: Nothing counted.
not_here.line: No total of what was asked or what was given, no list of who helped, and no wall of thank-yous.

not_here.name: Nobody at the front.
not_here.line: No professionals, no caseworkers, no intake and no forms. The only expertise in the room is having been there.

not_here.name: Nobody owes an answer.
not_here.line: An ask can go unanswered and an offer can go untaken, and neither is a verdict on anybody. If an ask goes by, asking again is allowed.

not_here.name: Not a crisis line.
not_here.line: Our [Help page](https://stimpunks.org/help/) is a set of doors, and [Coping](https://stimpunks.org/fieldguide/coping/#h-crisis-hotlines) lists crisis lines and warmlines. Nobody here is on call.
